key_insight: For proton ceramic fuel cell cathodes—not solar cells—increasing Y content from BCFZ to BCFY predicts a modest 5.3% proton-conductivity gain at 500 °C under operating gas conditions.
engineering_relevance: Cathode design should optimize both dopant composition and gas environment because proton transport depends on carrier concentration, mobility, and species.
method: Use ab initio molecular dynamics to compare proton tracer diffusivity across BCFZ, BCFZY0.1, and BCFY.
Model temperature-dependent proton concentrations using hydration, oxidation, and hydride-formation defect reactions.
Separate Y-doping effects on proton diffusivity and concentration.
evidence_signal: At 500 °C, the BCFZ-to-BCFY comparison predicts increases of 1.7% in proton diffusivity, 3.8% in proton concentration, and 5.3% in proton conductivity.
watch_item: The gains are computational predictions sensitive to gas conditions; at low oxygen partial pressure, the model predicts a shift from hydroxyl- to hydride-mediated proton transport.
paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
